solution: Factorise: \(1056 = 2^5 \times 3 \times 11\), \(1584 = 2^4 \times 3^2 \times 11\) and \(2178 = 2 \times 3^2 \times 11^2\). The common factors are \(2 \times 3 \times 11 = 66\).
Take the lower power of each common prime: \(2^2 \times 3^2 \times 5 = 180\).
The largest square tile has side \(\text{HCF}(1517, 902) = 41\) cm. The ceiling then takes \(\frac{1517}{41} \times \frac{902}{41} = 37 \times 22 = 814\) tiles.
The largest container that measures each amount exactly holds \(\text{HCF}(345, 120, 225) = 15\) L.
Remove the remainder 12: the number must divide 1344, 1856 and 2752. These are \(64 \times 21\), \(64 \times 29\) and \(64 \times 43\), so the largest such number is 64.
A number leaving the same remainder divides the differences \(73 - 25 = 48\), \(97 - 73 = 24\) and \(97 - 25 = 72\). Their HCF is 24.
Take the highest power of each prime: \(2^2 \times 3^3 \times 5 \times 11 = 5940\).
Factorise: \(7200 = 2^5 \times 3^2 \times 5^2\), \(1050 = 2 \times 3 \times 5^2 \times 7\), \(2100 = 2^2 \times 3 \times 5^2 \times 7\). The LCM is \(2^5 \times 3^2 \times 5^2 \times 7 = 50400\).
The bells toll together every \(\text{LCM}(9, 6, 4, 10, 8) = 360\) seconds. In an hour, 3600 seconds, that happens \(\frac{3600}{360} = 10\) times after the start.
The bells ring together every \(\text{LCM}(20, 30, 40) = 120\) minutes. Two hours after 11 am is 1 pm.
They meet at the start after \(\text{LCM}(42, 56, 63) = 504\) seconds.
The number is a multiple of \(\text{LCM}(10, 15, 18) = 90 = 2 \times 3^2 \times 5\). The smallest such multiple that is a perfect square needs another 2 and 5: \(90 \times 10 = 900 = 30^2\).
The sum must be a multiple of \(\text{LCM}(5, 6, 4, 3) = 60\). The next multiple after 2497 is 2520, so 23 must be added.
The HCF of fractions is \(\frac{\text{HCF of numerators}}{\text{LCM of denominators}} = \frac{\text{HCF}(5, 10, 25)}{\text{LCM}(6, 18, 36)} = \frac{5}{36}\).
The LCM of fractions is \(\frac{\text{LCM of numerators}}{\text{HCF of denominators}} = \frac{\text{LCM}(1, 5, 2, 4)}{\text{HCF}(3, 6, 9, 27)} = \frac{20}{3}\).
The product of two numbers equals HCF times LCM, so the other number is \(\frac{18 \times 3780}{540} = 126\).
With HCF 4 the numbers are \(3 \times 4 = 12\) and \(4 \times 4 = 16\). Their LCM is \(4 \times 3 \times 4 = 48\).
HCF times LCM equals the product of the numbers, so their product is 24. Two numbers with product 24 and difference 2 are 6 and 4.
Let the numbers be \(2k\) and \(3k\). Their product equals HCF times LCM, so \(6k^2 = 33750\), \(k = 75\), and the sum is \(5k = 375\).

solution: The HCF divides every number, so it must divide the LCM \(9570 = 2 \times 3 \times 5 \times 11 \times 29\). Of the options only 11 divides 9570.
Let the numbers be \(3k\), \(4k\) and \(5k\), whose LCM is \(60k = 2400\). So \(k = 40\), and the HCF is \(k = 40\).
Such numbers are multiples of \(\text{LCM}(21, 35, 63) = 315\). Below 10000 there are \(\left\lfloor \frac{9999}{315} \right\rfloor = 31\) of them.
The LCM of two numbers is always a multiple of their HCF. 60 is not a multiple of 8, so it can never be their LCM.
The biggest measure is \(\text{HCF}(403, 434, 465)\). Since these are \(31 \times 13\), \(31 \times 14\) and \(31 \times 15\), it is 31 kg.
The number is 5 more than a multiple of \(\text{LCM}(24, 30, 54) = 1080\). The least is \(1080 + 5 = 1085\).
Each remainder is 6 less than its divisor, so the number is 6 less than a multiple of \(\text{LCM}(20, 25, 35, 40) = 1400\). The least is \(1400 - 6 = 1394\).
The number is \(3600k + 4\), with \(3600 = \text{LCM}(16, 18, 20, 25)\). Since \(3600 \equiv 2 \pmod 7\), we need \(2k + 4 \equiv 0 \pmod 7\), so \(k = 5\). The number is \(18000 + 4 = 18004\).
The number is 4 more than a multiple of \(\text{LCM}(16, 24, 36) = 144\). The largest 4-digit multiple of 144 is \(69 \times 144 = 9936\), so the number is 9940.

The sum must be a multiple of \(\text{LCM}(15, 20, 24, 27, 32, 36) = 4320\). The largest sum reachable with a 5-digit addition is below \(8321 + 99999 = 108320\), and the largest multiple of 4320 there is \(25 \times 4320 = 108000\). So the number to add is \(108000 - 8321 = 99679\).
The number is a multiple of \(\text{LCM}(12, 18, 21, 28) = 252\). The least 4-digit multiple is \(4 \times 252 = 1008\).
The devices beep together every \(\text{LCM}(48, 72, 108) = 432\) seconds, which is 7 minutes 12 seconds. So the next time is 10:07:12.
